symptoms: The plant grows a hollow tube that looks like an onion leaf.
You may see a silvery white tube called a silver shoot.
The infested tiller stops growing new leaves.
The plant fails to produce any grain heads.
Leaves may look deformed, wilted, or rolled.
favourable_conditions: The pest population grows quickly during cloudy or rainy weather.
prevention: Plant your crop early in the season.
Choose varieties that are resistant or tolerant to this pest.
Keep field bunds clean and free of weeds.
Avoid planting the whole area at different times.
Use potash fertilizer at the recommended rate.
practices: Drain the water from your fields for 5 to 7 days.
Collect and destroy any plants that show signs of damage.
Set up light traps in the evening to catch adult flies.
Monitor the field for silver shoots and take action if 10 percent of tillers are affected.

organic_bio.text: Neem cake @ 100 kg during the time of last ploughing
